title: A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A Nature Biotechnology Comment by Thomas Burger, Xinzhou Ge and Jingyi Jessica Li proposes a 2 × 2 matrix to help sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers pick the right family of false discovery rate (FDR) procedures, or more rigorous alternatives, based on data and study design. The captured text is only the subscription preview (abstract, references, affiliations), so this card is light despite the raw record being marked not paywalled.

themes.theme: 2 × 2 taxonomy for choosing FDR procedures in omics

insights.claim: A Nature Biotechnology Comment proposes a 2 × 2 matrix that helps sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers choose the appropriate family of false discovery rate (FDR) control procedures depending on their data and study design.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Standardizing FDR method choice across genomics and proteomics could improve reproducibility of discoveries that feed biomarker and drug-target pipelines.
insights.quote: This Comment proposes a 2 × 2 matrix that helps sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers choose the appropriate family of FDR procedures
insights.locator: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central

insights.claim: Although false discovery rate control is central to omics research, the many FDR procedures in use rely on different statistical assumptions, implying that a mismatched procedure can undermine the validity of reported discoveries.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Omics-derived hits (targets, biomarkers) may carry hidden false-positive risk when the FDR method's assumptions don't fit the data, a diligence point for platform-biotech claims.
insights.quote: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central to omics research, yet the diverse procedures used rely on different assumptions.
insights.locator: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central

insights.claim: The authors of a Nature Biotechnology Comment on omics statistics argue that, depending on data and study design, alternative methods to standard FDR procedures may be more rigorous.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Signals potential shifts in accepted statistical practice for omics analysis software and pipelines, relevant to bioinformatics tool vendors and data-driven discovery firms.
